title: Translation by a point with bijective source and target is an automorphism of the arrow scheme

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 1328-1340

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: For a groupoid scheme over a field with U = Spec(k), if the point r of R has s and t inducing isomorphisms k to kappa(r), then the translation x maps to c(r, x) is an automorphism of R carrying the identity section e to r. The proof spells the functorial argument out completely: it builds the source section a and target section b of r with the relation a s b = b, defines the translation on T-valued points with a definedness check, defines the candidate inverse using the inverse map i of the groupoid with its own definedness check, and verifies both composite chase computations collapse to the identity via the groupoid axioms and the shown relation (source lines 1342-1406)

core_obligations: Construct the source section a : U -> R with s a = id (exists because s : k -> kappa(r) is an isomorphism by hypothesis) and the target section b with t b = id, and note b = a (t a)^{-1} so a s b = b (proof lines 1345-1351).
Define the translation morphism on T-valued points by f maps to c(a t f, f) and check definedness via s a = id (proof lines 1354-1360); note the translation sends e to a.
Define the candidate inverse on T-valued points by g maps to c(i b t g, g), where i is the inverse map of the groupoid, and check definedness via t b = id (proof lines 1363-1369).
Chase the composite in one direction: c(a t c(i b t g, g), c(i b t g, g)) = c(b t g, c(i b t g, g)) = c(c(b t g, i b t g), g) = c(e, g) = g, using a s b = b (proof lines 1371-1388).
Chase the composite in the other direction to get c(e, f) = f, using b = a (t a)^{-1} (proof lines 1390-1404).
Conclude the translation is an automorphism of R with e mapping to r (proof line 1405).
proof_roadmap: Build the sections a, b and the relation a s b = b (proof lines 1345-1351).
Define translation and candidate inverse with definedness checks (proof lines 1354-1369).
Two explicit chase computations give both composites equal to the identity (proof lines 1371-1404).
